families.name: The Pulse Suite
families.blurb: Six siblings drawn as living silicon. One visual language for everything the machine is doing to itself.

families.name: The AI Desk
families.blurb: What the agents on this machine are actually doing, and what they are costing.

families.name: Workspace Control
families.blurb: Hyprland workspaces that name themselves, pack themselves, and remember what belonged on them.

families.name: Media and Output
families.blurb: Sound and pixels leaving this machine for somewhere else in the house.

families.name: System and Desk
families.blurb: Everyday surfaces. Clipboard, clock, bluetooth, sleep, the car.

families.name: The Mac Bridge
families.blurb: Your phone and your Mac, in the Linux bar. The Mac is the gateway, this machine is the client, nothing is proxied through a stranger.

families.name: Infrastructure
families.blurb: The boring, load-bearing ones. Backups, exposed ports, latency, fleet health.

plugins.name: Disk Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living storage die.
plugins.description: A living storage die: free space, read and write throughput, drive busy time, I/O pressure, drive temperature and SMART health, btrfs allocation, seven-day history, and focus-only disk hogs.

plugins.name: PR Hunter
plugins.tagline: Open pull requests, and the workspace to deal with them.
plugins.description: GitHub pull requests and issues for Herdr and your saved projects, in the bar. Opens the right workspace or terminal and hands the work to an agent that is already running.

plugins.name: MenuBar Overload
plugins.tagline: Add as many plugins as you like.
plugins.description: The Omarchy bar with a dock-magnified carousel on each side. Add as many plugins as you like; roll through the ones that do not fit with the mouse wheel or a trackpad swipe, and each one pops out as it arrives.

plugins.name: Audio Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living audio chip.
plugins.description: A living audio chip: volume, mute, output picker and per-app mixer, drawn as a sibling of RAM Pulse, CPU Pulse and Net Pulse.

plugins.name: Net Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living network chip.
plugins.description: A living network chip: throughput, latency, Wi-Fi radio detail, interface settings, seven-day history, and focus-only top talkers.

plugins.name: CPU Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living processor die.
plugins.description: A living processor die: per-thread load, clocks, temperature, CPU pressure, seven-day history, and focus-only CPU hogs.

plugins.name: RAM Pulse
plugins.tagline: A living memory chip.
plugins.description: A living memory chip: continuous history, RAM pressure, swap and zram insight, and focus-only RAM hoarders.

issues.title: Offline review: 9 stability, installer and accounting findings, with 7 small PRs
issues.author: GreyforgeLabs

plugins.name: Power Pulse
plugins.tagline: Battery as a glowing flux cell whose colour is its charge.
plugins.description: Battery as a glowing flux cell whose colour is its charge: blue when full, yellow in the middle, red when low. A stream of glowing atoms rides in while charging, out on battery, with glints popping around them. Hour-long up and down power trace, live wattage, power profiles.

plugins.name: Sonomarchy
plugins.tagline: Every Sonos zone as a system audio output.
plugins.description: Makes every Sonos zone on your network a selectable system audio output, including legacy Play:1, Play:3, Play:5, Playbar and Connect speakers that have no AirPlay.

plugins.name: Chronos
plugins.tagline: A clock and calendar with a pulse.
plugins.description: Clock and calendar with a pulse: a day-progress ring, shimmering year and life rails, a drawn moon phase, and a month grid that arrives on a stagger.

plugins.name: Pastey
plugins.tagline: A clipboard that remembers.
plugins.description: A compact, searchable 200-item clipboard history for the Omarchy bar, with real screenshot thumbnails and the whole clip on hover.

plugins.name: Halo Bluetooth
plugins.tagline: A live sonar hero with battery halos.
plugins.description: Bluetooth with a live sonar hero, per-device battery halos and type-aware glyphs.

plugins.name: Tesla
plugins.tagline: Your car in the bar.
plugins.description: Your Tesla in the bar: where it is, how full it is, how far that gets you, and whether it is charging right now.

plugins.name: Blip
plugins.tagline: iMessage in the Omarchy bar.
plugins.description: iMessage in the Omarchy bar. Reads and sends through a Mac you own over a multiplexed SSH socket. iMessage is macOS-only, so this machine is a thin client and the Mac is the gateway. The bar badge counts every unread; desktop toasts fire only for handles on your allowlist, because chat.db is mostly bank alerts and 2FA codes.
